slides.headline: He was beaten by police for leading a protest. His death radicalized the generation that followed him.
Lala Lajpat Rai died on November 17, 1928, from injuries sustained in a police lathi-charge.
slides.body: Known as "Punjab Kesari" - the Lion of Punjab - Rai was leading a protest against the Simon Commission in Lahore on October 30, 1928, when police charged the demonstrators. He died 18 days later from his injuries.

slides.headline: His death pushed a new generation of revolutionaries toward direct action.
slides.body: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev - then young revolutionaries - held the police officer they blamed for Rai's death responsible, an episode that marked a turning point in their path toward the independence movement's more militant wing.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat still carries forward the resolve of people who paid for their protest with their lives.
slides.body: Lajpat Rai didn't live to see independence - but the anger his death provoked became part of the momentum that eventually got the country there.
